rationale: Source work to refine the active Candidate 0922502bc12a4af68ee74cb77942fd72 on the quorum arithmetic, recorded as feedback rather than a new obligation because the run is near its boundary. Two findings sharpen it. First, the applicability premise is now sourced: the code never rejects an even replica count. run.go:30 computes f = (len(c.ReplicaAddrs)-1)/2 and logs it without a parity check, and neither master/master.go nor config validates that the deployment has an odd number of replicas, so nothing in the captured files prevents N=4. Second, for even N the recovery threshold is strictly below a majority: SlowQuorumSize() = (N+1)/2 equals 2 for N=4 while a majority is N/2+1 = 3, and handlePrepareReply acts once len(lb.prepareReplies) >= SlowQuorumSize() (epaxos/epaxos.go:1210-1218), with the recovering leader's own reply included. So a recovering coordinator could collect a full slow quorum from replicas that never observed the value already committed elsewhere, which is exactly the intersection the fast path relies on; the fast path itself needs only preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize()-1 = 1 reply for N=4. The one protection that might still cover this is that the Accept phase needs a majority of Accept replies (acceptOKs+1 > N/2 in handleAcceptReply, epaxos/epaxos.go:1040), which for N=4 is 3 and therefore does intersect any 2-replica fast quorum; whether that is sufficient for every recovery branch (including the restart-with-NOOP branch taken when the slow quorum reports no state) is the next thing to read. I am not claiming a defect: the deployment examples use odd N and the branch-level argument is incomplete.

feedback.answered: The even-N applicability premise is grounded: no captured file validates that N is odd (run.go:30 computes f = (N-1)/2 with no parity check; master and config add none). For N=4, SlowQuorumSize() = 2 is below the majority of 3, and handlePrepareReply rebuilds once it has 2 replies including its own, so a recovery slow quorum need not intersect a 2-replica fast quorum. The slow Accept path's majority requirement (acceptOKs+1 > N/2 = 3 for N=4) is the candidate protection that would have to be shown sufficient.
remaining: Whether the restart-with-NOOP recovery branch (handlePrepareReply sub-cases 5/6) can commit a value for an instance already fast-committed by a disjoint 2-replica quorum when N is even.
